methods_ranked.name: MoCHi hard-negative mixing on the 4096 queue (Kalantidis et al., NeurIPS 2020)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: FULL TEXT (method section 4.1 and ablation text read via grep; not a complete sequential read). Gains reported on ImageNet-100 (MoCo-v2) and ImageNet-1K linear eval; no medical or derm data.
methods_ranked.mechanism: For each query q with queue Q (K negatives), sort negatives by q.n (descending) and keep the top-N hardest. Synthesize s extra negatives h_k = normalize(a_k n_i + (1 - a_k) n_j), with i, j sampled from the top-N, a_k ~ U(0,1). Append exp(q.h_k / T) to the softmax denominator. Cost is s dot products per query.
methods_ranked.exact_change: In the MoCo InfoNCE denominator (T=0.2), keep the 4096-key queue (already implemented in queue4096 arm). Compute top-N = 1024 hardest negatives per query by q.n. Sample s synthetic negatives per query: s = 128 for arm B1 (MoCHi(N=1024, s=128, s'=0)); s = 256 for arm B2 (MoCHi(N=1024, s=256, s'=0)). Keep positive pair, EMA 0.99, 2 views, batch 16, 6000 steps unchanged. Do not mix query-side features unless s' is defined and checked (see verify list).
methods_ranked.why_here: Our only positive arm is queue4096 (HAM +0.017 at 448D4). MoCHi is the direct, cheap extension of that exact arm: it spends the same memory on harder negatives. The brief's hypothesis (mel vs nevus confusers are near-duplicates in embedding space) matches the mechanism: MoCHi pushes the query away from its closest negatives, which are the hardest confusers. Paper reports MoCHi with K=4k matches MoCo-v2 with K=16k (ImageNet-100 ablation).

hyperparameters.s_prime: 0 for first arm; s' is the paper's query-side mixing count, definition to verify in paper sec 4.2 before coding

methods_ranked.expected_effect: ~30% chance of a seed-consistent HAM mel->NV reduction (>=1 pp) with macro-F1 non-decreasing (subjective prior, not measured). Largest risk: hard negatives include same-class (false) negatives, which push same-diagnosis lesions apart. This is why PhB-M2 should be run first or in the same arm.
methods_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_baseline: ~1.0x (s extra dot products per query; no extra forward passes). Not timed.
methods_ranked.risk: Pushes apart same-lesion/same-diagnosis near-duplicates present in ISIC 2019/2020 (no lesion_id). Overlap with FNC: the two must be ablated jointly or sequentially. Paper's sensitivity to N and s is reported on ImageNet-100 only.
methods_ranked.code: Official repo not verified. Paper states it builds on facebookresearch/moco (footnote 2, URL from paper text). Implement as a loss change in our existing queue path; unit-test the logits shape and the mix formula (RED first).
methods_ranked.predeclared_success_rule_for_run: Seed 42 exploratory vs same-environment queue4096+448D4 s42 baseline: PASS if HAM macro-F1 delta >= +0.005 AND HAM mel->NV delta <= -1.0 pp AND PAD macro-F1 delta >= -0.01. Seeds 43/44 confirm: PASS if HAM mel->NV delta <= 0 AND HAM macro-F1 delta >= 0 in both seeds. Checkpoints 2000, 4000, 6000 (mandatory). Multiplicity: report as a new arm in the log; no correction is applied to the gain claim beyond the rule.

methods_ranked.name: False-negative elimination on the queue (Huynh et al., 2022; code URL in abstract: github.com/google-research/fnc, not verified)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: FULL TEXT (sections 3.2.1, 3.2.2 and 4.1 read via grep). Ablations on ImageNet SimCLR v2 setup (batch 4096, 100 epochs). Threshold sensitivity: elimination is 'not very sensitive to thresholds' (Fig 4 right, text). Support-set construction (sec 3.2.3) NOT read in detail.
methods_ranked.mechanism: For anchor i, a candidate negative k is a false negative if its similarity to a support set S exceeds a threshold t (aggregation: mean or max over S; screening: threshold). False-negative elimination removes k from the denominator: L = -log exp(sim(z_i,z_j)/T) / sum_{k != i, k not in F_i} exp(sim(z_i,z_k)/T). Attraction variant (not first arm) moves F_i into the positive set.
methods_ranked.exact_change: CORRECTED (sec 3.2.3 read in full): support set S_i = additional augmented views of the SAME anchor image (not the queue, not other images). Per anchor: generate |S| extra views (paper: 'other support views from the same image besides the two main views'). Score each queue key m: score_m,i = aggregate_{s in S_i} cos(z_m, z_s), aggregate = mean (paper default option) or max. Candidate FN set F_i = keys with score_m,i > t (threshold screening; top-k is the alternative). Eliminate F_i from the denominator. Elimination only (attraction is sub-arm B2b). T=0.2, EMA 0.99 unchanged. Cost: |S| extra encoder forwards per anchor, NOT free (see cost).

hyperparameters.aggregation: mean over support (paper's default screening: threshold)
hyperparameters.support_set: other augmented views of the same anchor image (|S| extra views; |S| value not stated in the extracted text, choose 1-2 and report); NOT the queue
hyperparameters.attraction_variant: sub-arm only if elimination shows a signal

methods_ranked.why_here: Our SSL pool is ~34.7k images (see meta.verification_of_brief_claims) including multiple images per ISIC lesion, so false negatives in the 4096 queue are plausible and are never removed by the current loss. The sampler audit (0.49% same-component collisions) does not state whether it covered batch or queue negatives (not verified in the brief), so it does not rule out queue-level false negatives. The paper reports the gap from elimination grows with bigger crops (more shared content), which is our case of 224/448 global views of dermoscopy with heavy overlap.
methods_ranked.expected_effect: ~20-25% chance of a seed-consistent gain on HAM mel recall or mel->NV; effect likely small (paper: ~0.2% for elimination in its setup, ~1% total from FN count at 4096 negatives). Subjective prior.
methods_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_baseline: CORRECTED: ~1.0 + |S|/2 x encoder cost (each support view is an extra 224 forward through the student, no backward through it required only if detached; verify). With |S|=1 expect ~1.3-1.5x; NOT timed. The earlier ~1.0x assumed the queue as support and is void.
methods_ranked.risk: Mis-detected FNs (true hard negatives) removed; threshold depends on feature scale (448 features with row-L2). Interacts with PhB-M1 (both change negative set). Must log fraction of eliminated keys per step and check it is not ~0 or ~50%.
methods_ranked.code: URL from abstract only, not fetched. Implement from paper eq. (2).
methods_ranked.label_policy: Label-free. Lesion_id and diagnosis must NOT be used to detect FNs. Offline audit only: fraction of eliminated keys sharing diagnosis (diagnosis used only for audit, never in the loss).
methods_ranked.predeclared_success_rule_for_run: Same as PhB-M1 (seed 42 exploratory, 43/44 confirm), plus: eliminated fraction per step logged; arm reported as NULL-mechanism if eliminated fraction < 0.1%.

methods_ranked.name: Test-time registers on existing DINOv2 base features (training-free; Jiang et al. 2025, 2506.08010)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: ABSTRACT ONLY. Claims: training-free register-neuron shift yields cleaner attention and feature maps; results comparable to models trained with registers across downstream tasks.
methods_ranked.mechanism: Identify a sparse set of register neurons that concentrate high-norm activations on outlier tokens; shift those activations into an extra untrained token at inference. Removes high-norm artifact tokens that DINOv2 base shows in background regions.
methods_ranked.exact_change: Post-process frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 features at extraction time only (no training). Compare CLS4 features and cls4patch features with and without the test-time register on HAM dev and PAD dev, same readout (balanced LR, grouped CV). Keep 224 and 448 resolutions.
methods_ranked.hyperparameters: Neuron-selection rule and threshold from the paper (not read in full; verify before running). No new training hyperparameters.
methods_ranked.why_here: Cheap diagnostic of whether the artifact tokens we see at 448 px contribute to the CLS readout. Allowed under the brief (label-free feature post-processing, no diagnosis labels). Can be run as a single feature-extraction pass plus readouts.
methods_ranked.expected_effect: Low on CLS4 (~15% chance of a macro-F1 gain > 0.5 pp). Possibly larger on patch-level readouts. Subjective prior.
methods_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_baseline: ~0.05x (one forward pass per split, no training).
methods_ranked.risk: Post-hoc feature modification with selection on dev: multiplicity counts. Must be reported as a feature variant, not an SSL arm.
methods_ranked.predeclared_success_rule_for_run: Dev only. Positive only if HAM and PAD macro-F1 both improve by >= +0.005 in all 3 encoder seeds, with the paired group bootstrap CI excluding 0 on at least one dataset. Otherwise negative.

methods_ranked.name: Backbone fork: DINOv2-with-registers ViT-B/14 as the continued-MoCo init (public weights)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: Model existence VERIFIED on the Hub (facebook/dinov2-with-registers-base, Apache-2.0, 288.6K downloads, arXiv 2309.16588). Benefit for our task: ABSTRACT ONLY (Darcet et al. 2023; Jiang et al. 2025 abstract). A 2026 cross-architecture reproduction (2603.25803, abstract only) reports some claims do not generalize to all models.
methods_ranked.mechanism: Same DINOv2 family and objective, but trained with 4 extra register tokens that absorb high-norm artifact tokens. Starting point changes the dense/attention structure at 448 px.
methods_ranked.exact_change: Replace init with facebook/dinov2-with-registers-base (ViT-B/14 + 4 registers). Keep blocks 8-11 trainable, MoCo loss, queue4096 config for the new baseline (because queue4096 is the only positive arm) and plain 224 cls4 baseline. Refit baselines in the same environment for seeds 42/43/44.
methods_ranked.why_here: The brief keeps the encoder in DINOv2 family; registers are a family variant. Evidence in medical CXR (abstract, 2026 DINOv3 study W7212050844) shows that resolution-dependent gains matter most for small focal findings at 512 px; this supports testing the 448 path with a cleaner backbone. Requires new baseline set.
methods_ranked.expected_effect: Uncertain, direction unknown a priori (~35% chance of macro-F1 change > 0.5 pp in either direction).
methods_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_baseline: High: new 6000-step SSL run per seed (3 runs) plus new variant features and readouts. Not timed.
methods_ranked.risk: Breaks comparability with historical arms; a backbone fork is a real decision for project owner (keep comparability vs new base). Patch-size and register count checks needed before run.
methods_ranked.decision_for_lead: Real fork: keep DINOv2 (comparable, cheaper) vs test registers init (new baseline, more GPU). Present to project owner with this tradeoff; not recommended until PhB-M1/M2 are resolved.

methods_ranked.name: Hard-negative importance reweighting (Robinson et al., ICLR 2021, 2010.04592)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: ABSTRACT ONLY (search result). Claims: unsupervised hard-negative sampling with user-controlled hardness, no computational overhead, improves multiple modalities. Full text NOT read; hyperparameter names and values not verified.
methods_ranked.mechanism: Reweight negatives in the InfoNCE denominator by w_k proportional to exp(beta * q.n_k) (hardness parameter beta), a debiased-style estimator without labels.
methods_ranked.exact_change: Replace uniform negative weights in the 4096-queue denominator by normalized exp(beta q.n_k) weights. beta grid {0.5, 1.0} (to be verified in full text before coding).
methods_ranked.why_here: Overlaps with PhB-M1 (both emphasize hard negatives). Use only as the fallback if MoCHi fails, to test whether it is the hardness or the synthetic mixing that matters.
methods_ranked.expected_effect: Low-to-moderate, overlapping with PhB-M1 (~20% chance of seed-consistent gain). Subjective.
methods_ranked.risk: Without full text, the estimator's exact form and beta scale (dependence on T and feature norm) are unknown. Must read full text before implementation.

methods_ranked.name: Patch-level / local-global objectives (VICRegL 2210.01571; LOCA 2212.02400; JEM 2610.10013)
methods_ranked.evidence_level: ABSTRACT ONLY for all three. VICRegL: CNN, local-feature VICReg with geometric correspondence. LOCA (WACV 2024): patch clustering pseudo-labels + relative location. JEM (Oct 2026): patch-level student-teacher with info-theoretic terms, claims beats DINOv2 on segmentation at 300M-7B scale.
methods_ranked.mechanism: Add a dense patch-to-patch alignment loss between two views (correspondence via geometry or patch clustering) to improve patch-level features used by cls4patch/448 readouts.
methods_ranked.exact_change: Not specified to implementation level: each method needs a new loss path (correspondence mask or patch-cluster targets). Recommend not implementing before PhB-M1/M2 and PhB-M3.
methods_ranked.why_here: Our best patch readouts are 448 cls4patch (HAM 0.626) but cls4patch at 224 is worse (0.604); a patch objective may close that gap. CLS4 readout (the endpoint) likely changes little.
methods_ranked.expected_effect: Low on CLS4 (~10-15%); uncertain on patch readouts. Subjective.
methods_ranked.gpu_cost_vs_baseline: Medium-high: extra loss, patch matching, possibly extra forward. Not timed.
methods_ranked.risk: Abstract-only evidence; no verified code; JEM is 2026 and large-scale. Implementation risk high for our time budget.

candidates.name: Cosine temperature schedule for InfoNCE (Kukleva et al., ICLR 2023)
candidates.evidence_level: FULL TEXT (grep-extracted). Gains on CIFAR10/100-LT and ImageNet100-LT with MoCo and SimCLR (kNN and linear). Our brief tested constant temperature arms (negative) but NOT a time-varying schedule.
pseudocode: # per step s (converted from epochs, see below); tau_minus=0.1, tau_plus=1.0 (paper default)
logits = q . k / tau  (queue + positive, as in our MoCo code; replace fixed T=0.2)
loss = cross_entropy(logits, label=0)  # unchanged MoCo loss
candidates.paper_defaults: Eq. (5): tau_cos(t) = (tau+ - tau-) * (1 + cos(2 pi t / T)) / 2 + tau-, t in epochs. Default T=400 epochs, tau+=1.0, tau-=0.1. Paper also tests tau- in {0.07, 0.1, 0.2} and tau+ in {0.2,...,1.0} (Table 4) and linear oscillation in [0.1,0.5] every 200 epochs (Table 5). Optimizer for their runs: SGD, wd 1e-4, lr 0.5 cosine with 10-epoch warmup; MoCo dictionary 10000, projection 128, one linear layer; SimCLR batch 512. These are from-scratch LT settings, not continued pretraining; do not copy the optimizer.
candidates.critical_conversion_for_our_run: Paper period T is in EPOCHS (400 epochs in runs of 800-2000 epochs). Our run is 6000 steps x batch 16 = 96k samples over a 34,754-row pool = ~2.8 epochs. A 400-epoch period would never complete. Use step-based period P: propose P=2000 steps (3 cycles in 6000) with tau-=0.1, tau+=0.5 (paper alternative range), seed 42 exploratory. Paper reports robustness to T in 400-4000 epochs, so 3 cycles is a stronger test than the paper's, not a copy of it.
candidates.checkpoint_warning: Paper appendix A.1: performance depends on relative position within a period, and they select checkpoints by validation. Our checkpoints 2000/4000/6000 land at different cosine phases (2000 = max tau for P=2000 steps; 4000 = max again; 6000 = max again). Predeclare: report checkpoint 6000 only as primary (phase = end of cycle, tau = tau+). Mark 2000/4000 as descriptive.
candidates.why_here: Two-stage in-run schedule alternates instance discrimination (small tau) and group discrimination (large tau). The brief's constant T=0.2 arm is negative; a cycle is a different intervention. For long-tail data, the paper's argument is that tail classes benefit from instance discrimination; our endpoints are tail-like (mel, SCC).
candidates.expected_effect: Low-to-moderate, ~15-20% chance of seed-consistent gain (subjective). Risk: with queue4096 and tau near 0.1, similar-to-constant behaviour or instability.

candidates.name: Debiased contrastive loss (Chuang et al., NeurIPS 2020; official code chingyaoc/DCL)
candidates.evidence_level: FULL TEXT (sections 4-5, Fig 3). Gains on CIFAR10, STL10 (SimCLR), sentence embeddings, and RL; no medical or dermoscopy evidence; Fig 4 shows M=1 variant is trained on the same batch as biased baseline.
pseudocode: # x: anchor embedding (L2-normalized), x_plus: positive view (M=1), u_1..u_N: negatives from p (our queue/batch)
pos = exp(x . x_plus / t)            # t = temperature
neg = sum_i exp(x . u_i / t)          # i = 1..N
Ng  = max( (-N * tau_plus * pos + neg) / (1 - tau_plus),  N * exp(-1/t) )
candidates.paper_defaults: Official Fig. 3 pseudocode (lines 8-9 read verbatim; the definitions of pos and neg are the standard exp(sim/t) reading, verify against the figure's line 7 in the PDF). Temperature t=0.5 for CIFAR10/STL10 SimCLR (following SimCLR); latent dim 128; Adam lr 1e-3; 400 epochs; evaluation by linear classifier. tau_plus (class prior) is a hyperparameter with values tested in {0.005, 0.01, 0.1}; the paper says tau_plus can be estimated from data or treated as a hyperparameter. Estimator clamp: g >= exp(-1/t). M positives can be increased (their Fig 4c: M=1,2,4,8).
candidates.label_policy: tau_plus is the class prior of same-class negatives. Estimating it from labels would violate the brief. Use it only as a fixed hyperparameter (sweep 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.1 on seed 42 dev). State this explicitly in the report. With M=1 (only our second augmented view), no positive from p+ is available, so the correction works only on the negative term.
candidates.why_here: Corrects the sampling bias of negatives: a fraction of our queue negatives is same-class (ISIC has multiple images per lesion; mel vs nevus is a visually close pair). Alternative to FNC elimination (PhB-M2): soft correction, no threshold, cost 1.0x.
candidates.expected_effect: Low-to-moderate, overlapping FNC and MoCHi. ~15-20% chance of seed-consistent gain (subjective).
candidates.risk: The paper's gains are on SimCLR with batch 256-4096 and CIFAR-scale data; with queue4096 and T=0.2 the clamp term may dominate. Must log the fraction of samples hitting the clamp.

candidates.name: DINOv2-native objective continuation (DINO + iBOT + KoLeo + SK centering) instead of MoCo (Oquab et al. 2024; ExPLoRA recipe)
candidates.evidence_level: FULL TEXT for DINOv2 (objective, KoLeo, hyperparameters). ExPLoRA (ICML 2025, full text grep): continued pre-training on a new domain should use the SAME unsupervised loss used to train W_S (their finding, section 3, 'we find that using the same unsupervised loss C_S as was used for W_S is beneficial'); DINOv2 continuation in ExPLoRA reaches +9.3 pp linear probe over DINOv2 ViT-L on fMoW (Table 2, satellite, not dermatology).
candidates.why_here: Our continued pretraining replaces the native DINOv2 objective with MoCo. ExPLoRA's ablation suggests the objective mismatch is a candidate cause of the ceiling we see. This is the most direct test of whether the MoCo choice is the bottleneck. Label-free.
pseudocode: # student s, teacher t = EMA(s); heads: DINO head h_d, iBOT head h_i (separate, untied)
# two global crops (224) + local crops (98), per sample
L_dino = mean_{crops} CE( softmax((h_d(t_cls)-c)/tau_t) , softmax(h_d(s_cls)/tau_s) )   # c: centering (SK or moving average)
L_ibot = mean_{masked i} CE( softmax((h_i(t_patch_i)-c')/tau_t) , softmax(h_i(s_patch_i)/tau_s) )  # student masked, teacher unmasked
L_koleo = -(1/n) sum_i log( min_{j!=i} || l2norm(x_i) - l2norm(x_j) || )   # on class tokens of first global crop
# teacher: EMA with momentum m_t cosine 0.994 -> 1.0; SK centering 3 iterations (teacher), softmax (student)
default_hyperparameters_DINOv2_appendix_: AdamW, weight decay cosine 0.04 -> 0.2, no weight decay in ExPLoRA continuation (their C.1)
Learning rate: 1e-3 for ViT-B/14 distilled, batch 2048 (Table 16 row); ExPLoRA continuation used base lr 2e-3, batch 1024 effective (32 x 32 grad accum), 200k iterations, linear warmup + cosine
Teacher temperatures: warmup 0.04 and final 0.07 (ExPLoRA C.1 paraphrase of DINOv2 defaults; primary DINOv2 text does not list the value; verify in Table 16 of the PDF)
Crops: global 224 (>32% of image), local 98 (5-32%); KoLeo weight 0.1 on first global crop
iBOT mask ratio: 0.1-0.5, half of samples masked (ExPLoRA C.1)
Linear DINO-iBOT head: 3 layers, bottleneck 256, hidden 2048, out 65536; head frozen first 3k iterations (ExPLoRA C.1; DINOv2 publishes no DINO/iBOT heads, so heads are re-initialised)
Sinkhorn-Knopp 3 iterations on teacher; untied DINO and iBOT heads (DINOv2 Sec 4)
candidates.critical_caveat: DINOv2 public checkpoints do not include DINO or iBOT heads (ExPLoRA C.1). Heads are trained from scratch, so the native objective starts from a random head against a strong backbone: a head warm-up (frozen 3k iterations, as ExPLoRA) is required. Also, this changes the objective from the MoCo loss described in the brief; treat as a new arm, not a MoCo hyperparameter.
candidates.cost: Higher than MoCo: teacher and student forward on 2 global + local crops, plus masked student forward for iBOT. Estimate ~1.5-2.5x per step; NOT timed. Measure 50 steps before scheduling.
candidates.risk: Large objective change; fails silently if head warm-up or EMA schedule is wrong. Requires a unit test on the loss with a fixed seed (RED first).

candidates.note: MoCHi (2010.01028) full text confirmed; default hyperparameters for MoCo-v2 on ImageNet-100 in the paper: lr 0.03, batch 128 (ImageNet-100) and 256 (ImageNet-1K), embedding dim 128, cosine lr schedule, pretraining 100 epochs taken from 200-epoch run checkpoint. The main MoCHi tuple (N, s, s') examples in Fig 3a: (1024,128,256), (1024,256,512), (1024,1024,128). The MoCHi default configuration was not identified with certainty; use (1024,128,0) as the seed-42 exploratory arm and verify s' definition before coding.

RESOLVED. FNC sec 3.2.3 read: support set = other augmented views of the anchor image; screening by aggregated similarity of negatives to those views; threshold or top-k. The queue-as-support proxy in PhB-M2 was WRONG and is replaced. Cost rises with |S| extra encoder forwards per anchor.

RESOLVED. MoCHi sec 4.2: s' synthetic hard negatives mix the QUERY with a random hardest negative: h' = normalize(beta*q + (1-beta)*n_j), beta ~ U(0, 0.5), n_j from the top-N set; computed in the loss space (after the 2-layer MLP head). Extra cost ~ s' dot products. Paper Sec 4.3: s'=0 (negative-negative mixing only) keeps final proxy-task difficulty near MoCo-v2; s'>0 makes the proxy harder. Default (N,s,s') used in the paper's main results is still not confirmed; Fig 3a sweeps (N,s) with N up to 16384 and s in {128..1024}. Run B1 = (1024,128,0); optional B3 = (1024,128,256) on the paper's sweep grid.
